title: Leonardo da Vinci
subtitle: Portraits, sacred works and notebooks, 1472–1519
intro:
Fifteen works by Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519), from the early *Annunciation* to the late *Saint John the Baptist*. They hang in three rooms at true scale where the walls allow. The *Last Supper* is a mural in Milan and appears here as a full-size reproduction.

Images: public-domain photographs via Wikimedia Commons. Provenance notes are condensed from the holding museums' published records.

artworks.title: Mona Lisa (La Gioconda)
artworks.credit: Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures

provenance.event: Begun in Florence, probably a portrait of Lisa Gherardini, wife of Francesco del Giocondo
Kept by Leonardo, who took it to France
French royal collection under Francis I
Placed in the new Musée du Louvre
Hung in Napoleon's bedroom at the Tuileries
Stolen from the Louvre by Vincenzo Peruggia; recovered in Florence
Returned to the Louvre

artworks.rights: Public domain (photograph: C2RMF, via Wikimedia Commons)
artworks.description: Probably the most famous painting in the world. Leonardo kept working on it for years, building the soft transitions of light and shade (*sfumato*) from thin glazes. The landscape behind the sitter does not quite line up on the two sides of her head.

artworks.title: Lady with an Ermine
artworks.credit: Princes Czartoryski Foundation, National Museum in Kraków

provenance.event: Painted in Milan; the sitter is identified as Cecilia Gallerani, companion of Ludovico Sforza
Bought in Italy by Prince Adam Jerzy Czartoryski for his mother Izabela's collection at Puławy
Hidden and moved to Paris after the November Uprising; later returned to Kraków
Seized during the German occupation; recovered by the Allies in 1945
Czartoryski collection acquired by the Polish state

artworks.rights: Public domain (Google Art Project, via Wikimedia Commons)
artworks.description: One of only four surviving portraits of women by Leonardo. The turn of the sitter, echoed by the alert ermine (a Sforza emblem and a pun on Gallerani's name, Greek *galê*), was a radically new way of making a portrait move.

artworks.title: Ginevra de' Benci

provenance.event: Painted in Florence, probably around Ginevra's marriage to Luigi Niccolini
Princes of Liechtenstein, Vienna and later Vaduz
Purchased by the National Gallery of Art
provenance.note: The only painting by Leonardo in the Americas

artworks.rights: Public domain (Google Art Project, via Wikimedia Commons)
artworks.description: Leonardo's earliest known portrait. The juniper bush behind the sitter (*ginepro*) plays on her name. The panel was cut down at the bottom, probably removing her hands.

artworks.title: La Belle Ferronnière

provenance.event: Painted in Milan; the sitter may be Lucrezia Crivelli
French royal collection, recorded at Fontainebleau
Musée du Louvre

artworks.rights: Public domain (Google Arts & Culture, via Wikimedia Commons)
artworks.description: The title comes from a later confusion with a mistress of Francis I who was married to an ironmonger (*ferronnier*). The parapet in the foreground and the sitter's sideways glance hold the viewer at a distance.

artworks.title: Presumed Self-Portrait

provenance.event: Drawn, probably in Milan
Acquired by King Charles Albert of Sardinia for the Biblioteca Reale, Turin

artworks.rights: Public domain (Web Gallery of Art, via Wikimedia Commons)
artworks.description: Long accepted as Leonardo's only self-portrait, though some scholars think it shows an older man drawn earlier. It is very fragile and rarely shown.

artworks.title: Annunciation

provenance.event: Painted in Verrocchio's workshop, Florence
Monastery of San Bartolomeo at Monteoliveto, near Florence
Transferred to the Uffizi

artworks.rights: Public domain (Google Art Project, via Wikimedia Commons)
artworks.description: An early work, still partly in the manner of Verrocchio's workshop. The perspective is calculated for a viewer standing to the right and below, which explains the oddly long right arm of the Virgin when seen straight on.

artworks.title: Virgin of the Rocks
artworks.medium: Oil on panel, transferred to canvas

provenance.event: Commissioned by the Confraternity of the Immaculate Conception, San Francesco Grande, Milan
Probably left Milan for France; replaced by a second version, now in London
Recorded at Fontainebleau in the French royal collection
Musée du Louvre

artworks.title: Adoration of the Magi

provenance.event: Commissioned by the Augustinian friars of San Donato a Scopeto
Left unfinished when Leonardo moved to Milan; kept in the house of Amerigo de' Benci
Medici collections
Uffizi
Restored by the Opificio delle Pietre Dure

artworks.rights: Public domain (Google Art Project, via Wikimedia Commons)
artworks.description: Never finished, so it shows how Leonardo built a picture: the underdrawing and brown underpainting reveal a swirl of figures around the Virgin and, behind them, ruined architecture and fighting horsemen.

artworks.title: Saint John the Baptist

provenance.event: Probably among the works with Leonardo in France at his death
Given by Louis XIII to Charles I of England
Sold after Charles I's execution; bought by the banker Everhard Jabach
Acquired by Louis XIV
Musée du Louvre

artworks.rights: Public domain (photograph: C2RMF, via Wikimedia Commons)

artworks.title: The Virgin and Child with Saint Anne

provenance.event: Unfinished in Leonardo's studio at his death
Acquired in Casale Monferrato by Cardinal Richelieu
Given by Richelieu to Louis XIII
Cleaned and restored at the Louvre

artworks.rights: Public domain (photograph: C2RMF, via Wikimedia Commons)

artworks.title: The Baptism of Christ

artist.name: Andrea del Verrocchio and Leonardo da Vinci

provenance.event: Painted in Verrocchio's workshop for the Vallombrosan monastery of San Salvi, Florence
Transferred to the Accademia, Florence
Uffizi

artworks.description: According to Vasari, the young Leonardo painted the angel on the far left so well that Verrocchio gave up painting. The softly modelled angel and the hazy landscape are usually given to Leonardo.

artworks.title: The Last Supper
artworks.medium: Tempera and oil on gesso, pitch and mastic (mural); shown as a reproduction
artworks.collection: Refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan

provenance.event: Commissioned by Ludovico Sforza, Duke of Milan, for the convent refectory
Already deteriorating because of Leonardo's experimental technique
Refectory used by Napoleonic troops
Refectory bombed; the mural survived behind sandbags
Restoration led by Pinin Brambilla Barcilon

artworks.description: The moment just after Christ says that one of the apostles will betray him. Leonardo groups the twelve in threes and makes the vanishing point of the room fall on Christ's head.

artworks.title: Vitruvian Man
artworks.medium: Pen and ink with wash over metalpoint on paper

provenance.event: Inherited with Leonardo's papers by Francesco Melzi
Collection of the painter Giuseppe Bossi, Milan
Acquired by the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice

artworks.rights: Public domain (photograph: Luc Viatour, via Wikimedia Commons)
artworks.description: An illustration of the proportions of the human body described by the Roman architect Vitruvius. The figure fits both a circle and a square, with the navel and the groin as their respective centres.

artworks.title: Studies of the Foetus in the Womb
artworks.medium: Red and black chalk, pen and ink wash on paper

provenance.event: Inherited by Francesco Melzi
Sculptor Pompeo Leoni, who bound the anatomical sheets into an album
English Royal Collection

artworks.rights: Public domain (photograph: Luc Viatour, via Wikimedia Commons)

artworks.title: Head of a Woman (La Scapigliata)
artworks.medium: Umber, green amber and white lead on poplar panel
artworks.collection: Complesso Monumentale della Pilotta, Galleria Nazionale, Parma

provenance.event: Possibly the work recorded in the Gonzaga collection, Mantua, in 1627
Acquired for the gallery in Parma

rooms.name: Portraits
rooms.description: Four women painted in Florence and Milan, and the face of the artist himself.

rooms.name: Sacred Works
rooms.description: Altarpieces from the workshop years in Florence to the late works in France.

rooms.name: The Refectory and the Notebooks
rooms.description: The Last Supper at full size, opposite drawings from Leonardo's notebooks.
